'''Shou-Wu Zhang''' ({{lang-zh|c= 张寿武|p=Zhāng Shòuwǔ}}; born October 9, 1962) is a Chinese-American mathematician known for his work in [[number theory]] and [[arithmetic geometry]]. He is currently a professor of mathematics at [[Princeton University]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
Shou-Wu Zhang was born in [[Hexian]], [[Ma'anshan]], [[Anhui]], [[China]], on October 9, 1962.<ref name="amss">{{cite web|url=http://www.amss.ac.cn/xwdt/zhxw/2011/201111/t20111111_3394825.html |title=从放鸭娃到数学大师 |trans-title=From ducklings to mathematics master |publisher=Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science |date=11 November 2011 |accessdate= 5 May 2019 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="dream">{{cite web|url=https://news.sina.com.tw/article/20190503/31155020.html |title=專訪張壽武：在數學殿堂里，依然懷抱小學四年級的夢想  |trans-title=Interview with Zhang Shou-Wu: In the mathematics department, he still has his dream from fourth grade of elementary school |publisher=Beijing Sina Net |date=3 May 2019 |accessdate= 5 May 2019 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="hx-gov">{{cite web|url=http://www.hx.gov.cn/content/detail/59fb250a9e8b43880f0056a8.html |title=旅美青年数学家张寿武 |trans-title=Zhang Shouwu, a young mathematician in the United States |publisher=He County Government |date=2 November 2017 |accessdate= 5 May 2019 |language=zh}}</ref> Zhang grew up in a poor farming household and could not attend school until eighth grade [[Cultural Revolution#Academics and education|due to the Cultural Revolution]].<ref name="amss"/> He spent most of his childhood raising ducks in the countryside and self-studying mathematics textbooks that he acquired from [[sent-down youth]] in trades for frogs.<ref name="amss"/><ref name="dream"/> By the time he entered junior high school at the age of fourteen, he had taught himself calculus and had become interested in number theory after reading about [[Chen Jingrun]]'s proof of [[Chen's theorem]] which made substantial progress on [[Goldbach's conjecture]].<ref name="amss"/><ref name="dream"/><ref name="sina">{{cite web|url=http://edu.sina.com.cn/l/2019-05-04/doc-ihvhiqax6533865.shtml |title=专访数学家张寿武：要让别人解中国人出的数学题 |trans-title=Interview with mathematician Zhang Shouwu: Let others solve the math problems of Chinese people |publisher=Sina Education |date=4 May 2019 |accessdate= 5 May 2019 |language=zh}}</ref>

===Education===
Zhang was admitted to the [[Sun Yat-sen University]] chemistry department in 1980 after scoring poorly on his mathematics entrance examinations, but he later transferred to the mathematics department after feigning [[color blindness]] and received his bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1983.<ref name="ims">{{cite magazine|last=Leong |first=Y. K. |date=July–December 2018 |url=https://ims.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/imprints-32-2018.pdf |title=Shou-Wu Zhang: Number Theory and Arithmetic Algebraic Geometry |issue=32 |magazine=Imprints |pages=32–36 |publisher=The Institute for Mathematical Sciences, National University of Singapore |access-date=5 May 2019}}</ref><ref name="amss"/><ref name="dream"/><ref name="hx-gov"/><ref name="sina"/><ref name="zhihu"/> He then studied under analytic number theorist [[Wang Yuan (mathematician)|Wang Yuan]] at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] where he received his master's degree in 1986.<ref name="amss"/><ref name="sina"/><ref name="hx-gov"/><ref name="zhihu">{{cite web|url=https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/31700224 |title=专访数学家张寿武：数学苍穹闪烁中国新星 |trans-title=Interview with mathematician Zhang Shouwu: A new Chinese star flashing in the mathematical sky |publisher=Zhishi Fenzi |date=4 December 2017 |accessdate= 5 May 2019 |language=zh}}</ref> In 1986, Zhang was brought to the United States to pursue his doctoral studies at [[Columbia University]] by [[Dorian M. Goldfeld]].<ref name="amss"/><ref name="dream"/> He initially studied under Goldfeld and then [[Hervé Jacquet]],<ref name="ims"/> before deciding to work with [[Lucien Szpiro]], a visiting professor at Columbia at the time, and [[Gerd Faltings]] at Princeton University.<ref name="ims"/> He received his PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Szpiro in 1991.<ref name="ims"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=37832}}</ref>

===Career===
Zhang was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and an assistant professor at Princeton University from 1991 to 1996.<ref name="hx-gov"/><ref name="zhihu"/> In 1996, Zhang moved back to Columbia University where he was a tenured professor until 2013.<ref name="amss"/><ref name="ims"/><ref name="hx-gov"/><ref name="zhihu"/> He has been a professor at Princeton University since 2011<ref name="ims"/><ref name="zhihu"/> was named the Henry Burchard Fine Professor from 2014 to 2015,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2014/04/07/faculty-chosen-endowed-professorships |website=[[Princeton University]] |title=Faculty chosen for endowed professorships |author=Office of Communications |accessdate=March 21, 2021}}</ref> and was named a Eugene Higgins Professor in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2021/05/26/faculty-members-named-endowed-professorships |website=[[Princeton University]] |title=Faculty members named to endowed professorships |author=Office of Communications |accessdate=May 26, 2021}}</ref>

Zhang is on the editorial boards of: ''[[Acta Mathematica Sinica]]'', ''[[Algebra & Number Theory]]'', ''[[Forum of Mathematics]]'', ''[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]'', ''National Science Review'', ''Pure and Applied Mathematics Quarterly'', ''Science in China'', and ''Research in Number Theory''.<ref name="ims"/> He has previously served on the editorial boards of: ''[[Journal of Number Theory]]'', ''[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]'', ''Journal of Algebraic Geometry'', and ''[[International Journal of Number Theory]]''.<ref name="ims"/>

==Research==
Zhang's doctoral thesis ''Positive line bundles on Arithmetic Surfaces'' {{harvs|last=Zhang |year=1992}} proved a [[Ample line bundle#Intersection theory|Nakai–Moishezon type theorem]] in [[intersection theory]] using a result from [[differential geometry]] already proved in [[Tian Gang]]'s doctoral thesis.<ref name="ims"/> In a series of subsequent papers ({{harvs|nb|last=Zhang |year1=1993 |year2=1995a |year3=1995b}}, {{harvs|nb|last1=Szpiro |last2=Ullmo |last3=Zhang |year=1997}}), he further developed his theory of 'positive line bundles' in [[Arakelov theory]] which culminated in a proof of the [[Bogomolov conjecture]] with [[Emmanuel Ullmo]] and a further generalization of the Bogomolov conjecture ({{harvs|nb|last=Zhang |year=1998}}).<ref name="ims"/><ref>{{Citation |last=Ullmo |first=Emmanuel |title=Positivité et Discrétion des Points Algébriques des Courbes |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=147 |issue=1 |year=1998 |pages=167–179 |doi=10.2307/120987 |jstor=120987 | zbl=0934.14013 |arxiv=alg-geom/9606017 }}</ref>

In 2001, Zhang proved a generalization of the [[Gross–Zagier theorem]] to modular [[abelian varieties]] of [[General linear group|GL(2)]] type ({{harvs|nb|last=Zhang |year1=2001}}).<ref name="ims"/> In particular, the result led him to a proof of the rank one [[Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]] for modular abelian varieties of GL(2) type over [[Totally real number field|totally real field]]s through his work relating the [[Néron–Tate height]] of Heegner points to special values of [[L-function]]s in {{harvs|last=Zhang |year1=1997 |year2=2001}}.<ref name="ims"/><ref>{{cite journal|last=Zhang |first=Wei |title=The Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture and Heegner points: a survey |journal=Current Developments in Mathematics |volume=2013 |pages=169–203|doi=10.4310/CDM.2013.v2013.n1.a3 |year=2013 |doi-access=free }}.</ref> In 2013, Zhang and his former doctoral students [[Xinyi Yuan]] and [[Wei Zhang (mathematician)|Wei Zhang]] established a full generalization of the Gross–Zagier theorem to all [[Shimura variety|Shimura curve]]s ({{harvs|nb|last1=Yuan |last2=Zhang |last3=Zhang |first3=W. |year=2009}} {{harvs|nb|last1=Yuan |last2=Zhang |last3=Zhang |first3=W. |year=2013}}).

In [[arithmetic dynamics]], {{harvs|txt|last=Zhang |year1=1995a |year2=2006}} posed conjectures on the [[Zariski topology|Zariski density]] of non-fibered [[endomorphism]]s of [[Quasi-projective variety|quasi-projective varieties]] and {{harvs|txt|last1=Ghioca |last2=Tucker |last3=Zhang |year=2011}} proposed a dynamical analogue of the [[Arithmetic of abelian varieties#Manin–Mumford conjecture|Manin–Mumford conjecture]].<ref name="ad">{{cite journal|title=Current trends and open problems in arithmetic dynamics |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=56 |issue=4 |pages=611–685 |first1=Robert |last1=Benedetto |first2=Patrick |last2=Ingram |first3=Rafe |last3=Jones |first4= Michelle |last4=Manes |first5=Joseph H. |last5=Silverman |authorlink5=Joseph H. Silverman |first6=Thomas J. |last6=Tucker |doi=10.1090/bull/1665|year=2019 |arxiv=1806.04980 |s2cid=53550119 }}</ref><ref name="ims"/>

In 2018, {{harvs|txt|last1=Yuan |last2=Zhang |year=2018}} proved the [[Colmez conjecture|averaged Colmez conjecture]] which was shown to imply the [[André–Oort conjecture]] for [[Siegel modular form|Siegel modular varieties]] by [[Jacob Tsimerman]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |title=February 2018 |issn=1088-9477 |volume=65 |issue=2 |year=2018 |page=191}}</ref>

==Awards==
Zhang has received a [[Sloan Fellowship|Sloan Foundation Research Fellowship]] (1997) and a [[Morningside Gold Medal of Mathematics]] (1998). He is also a [[Clay Mathematics Institute|Clay Foundation Prize Fellow]] (2003), [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Foundation Fellow]] (2009), Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2011), and Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2016).<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2015-11-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/shou-wu-zhang/|title=Shou-Wu Zhang|publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation|accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref><ref name="ims"/>, Andrew Wiles Medal of [[International Congress of Basic Sciences]]. He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=&page=163 |title= ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers |accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref><ref name="ims"/><ref name="zhihu"/><ref>{{cite book|author=Zhang, Shou-Wu|chapter=Small points and Arakelov theory|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=217–225|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011657000}}</ref>
